correctness.rationale: The product Poisson law has positive mass at every finite nonnegative count vector; the one-location bound thus holds pointwise. An all-positive vector forces a singleton first atom, the stopping axiom forces that atom into all outputs and forces singleton output at each positive multiplicity. The zero fiber is an inherited stopping set and induction supplies every fixed-prefix rule uniquely. Explicit atomic jump times prove pointwise CTDT attainment; independent exact cylinder-cover enumeration agrees through four binary sites and three ternary sites.

originality.rationale: Relevant full source sections were inspected. Khezeli (2026) proves only the diffuse single-point attainability statement up to null modifications, and its atomic CTDT theorem assumes an already existent CTDT. Last–Peccati–Yogeshwaran (2021) furnish the axioms and generic nonattainability, not finite atomic complete normal forms. Targeted theorem-phrase searches and scientific literature comparisons did not reveal implication-level coverage. An implicit classical query-normal-form result remains possible.
residual_risks: The partial-permutation normal form may be implicit in classical finite sequential-query/decision-tree literature not surfaced by semantic search.
Full infinite atomic or diffuse exact attainability is not addressed.

value.rationale: A complete and intensity-independent exact classification of a natural constrained family of finite Poisson stopping sets resolves the atomic one-occupied-location analogue of a recent diffuse attainability problem. The uniqueness and formula \(\sum_{r=0}^n n!/(n-r)!\) quantify all valid rules; exact pointwise CTDT attainment and a two-location adaptive counterexample identify a sharp structural boundary.
